boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Howard University study settings, from reservable technology-equipped rooms to quiet campus spaces, with current access constraints noted.

cards.title: Bring the Whole Project Team
cards.subtitle: A six-seat, glass-enclosed room in Frederick Undergraduate Library
cards.notes: Reserve G045 when six seats, three round tables, and a shared screen suit the assignment; bring a device that can connect wirelessly.
cards.short_summary: The largest documented Frederick Library study room pairs three tables with a wall-mounted monitor.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University Libraries identifies G045 as a glass-enclosed study room for up to six people, with three round tables and a wirelessly accessible wall-mounted monitor.
cards.access_notes: Online reservation is limited to Howard University students. Bookings are 1–2 hours, with a maximum of 2 reserved hours per day.

cards.title: Put the Draft on the Big Screen
cards.subtitle: A five-seat collaboration room with flexible display connections
cards.notes: Choose G049 for a five-person review session, then connect to the wall monitor wirelessly or by HDMI so everyone can follow revisions.
cards.short_summary: A large shared table and dual connection options make G049 practical for collective editing.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University Libraries states that G049 seats five at a large table and provides ergonomic chairs plus a wall-mounted monitor with wireless or HDMI connectivity.
cards.access_notes: Howard students must reserve online. Reservations have a 1-hour minimum and a 2-hour daily maximum; unconfirmed reservations are canceled after 15 minutes.

cards.title: Rehearse Around One Table
cards.subtitle: Five ergonomic seats and a presentation display in Frederick Library
cards.notes: Book G048 for a small-group rehearsal or focused work block; use its generous table to keep laptops, notes, and handouts organized.
cards.short_summary: G048 supports presentation practice with seating for five and a screen visible from the shared table.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University Libraries describes G048 as a five-person room with a generous table, ergonomic seating, and a wall-mounted screen supporting wireless or HDMI connections.
cards.access_notes: Available by online reservation to Howard University students. A single student may reserve it, though the room is designed for group study.

cards.title: Work Through the Deck Together
cards.subtitle: A five-seat room with a wireless and HDMI-ready monitor
cards.notes: Use G047 when a shared display will keep a team aligned; reserve first and leave the furniture in place under library room rules.
cards.short_summary: This five-seat room combines ergonomic chairs, a large table, and straightforward screen sharing.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University Libraries lists G047 with a large table for five, ergonomic chairs, and a wall-mounted monitor that accepts wireless or HDMI connections.
cards.access_notes: Howard University students reserve the room online for 1–2 hours. Furniture cannot be moved into or out of study rooms.

cards.title: Settle In for a Focused Sprint
cards.subtitle: A technology-equipped room for groups of up to five
cards.notes: Reserve G046 for a concentrated project block, and bring an HDMI cable as a dependable alternative to its wireless monitor connection.
cards.short_summary: G046 offers a spacious work surface and two ways to share material on its presentation display.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University Libraries says G046 has a spacious table seating five, ergonomic chairs, and a wall-mounted display accessible wirelessly or by HDMI.
cards.access_notes: Online booking is restricted to Howard students. Conversations and equipment must not disturb people in adjacent rooms.

cards.title: Study Beside a Large Window
cards.subtitle: A daylight-facing, five-seat collaboration room
cards.notes: Pick G043 when natural light helps the session; gather up to five people around its table and share work on the wall display.
cards.short_summary: A large window distinguishes G043 from the library’s otherwise similarly equipped collaboration rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University Libraries documents G043 as a five-seat study room with a large window, ergonomic chairs, a large table, and a wireless- or HDMI-enabled wall display.
cards.access_notes: Howard University students may reserve the room online. Personal property cannot be left unattended to hold a reservation.

cards.title: Take the Window Seat as a Team
cards.subtitle: Natural light, five chairs, and a shared presentation monitor
cards.notes: Book G041 for collaborative work that benefits from daylight, then connect one laptop to the monitor so the table stays clear.
cards.short_summary: G041 combines a naturally lit setting with the standard five-person collaboration setup.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University Libraries describes G041 as a windowed room with natural light, a large five-seat table, ergonomic chairs, and a monitor supporting wireless or HDMI input.
cards.access_notes: Reserve online with Howard student credentials. Only one person or group may occupy the room at a time, and privacy is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Find a Quiet Area in Founders
cards.subtitle: Howard’s landmark main library and a documented quiet-study option
cards.notes: Enter with identification, ask library staff to point out a quiet area, and use the circulation desk when course reserves or stacks support the task.
cards.short_summary: Founders offers quiet study alongside circulating collections, course reserves, and research services.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard’s Office of Student Accessibility names Founders Library among the university’s quiet study spaces, while the library documents quiet areas and study services.
cards.source_title: Housing Accommodations Request | Howard University Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Howard libraries admit students, faculty, staff, alumni, and the public; visitors need government-issued photo ID and may need to sign in. Access can be restricted.

cards.title: Try a Quieter Academic Reset
cards.subtitle: A campus landmark officially identified as a quiet study space
cards.notes: Check the chapel’s current availability before settling in, keep noise low in the shared setting, and choose another space when programs are underway.
cards.short_summary: Rankin Chapel provides a distinctive quiet setting beyond Howard’s library study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University’s Office of Student Accessibility explicitly lists Rankin Chapel as one of the quiet study spaces available to all students, while noting shared-space noise may occur.
cards.source_title: Housing Accommodations Request | Howard University Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: The cited university guidance says the space is available to all students but is shared and not a formal accommodation. Confirm access around chapel programming.

cards.entity_name: Vernon E. Jordan Jr. Law Library
cards.title: Plug In at an Oak Reading Table
cards.subtitle: A professional-school library with power and data connections
cards.notes: Use an oak table when a long laptop session needs power and data access; verify Law Library entry eligibility before traveling from central campus.
cards.short_summary: Oak study tables with built-in connectivity give the Law Library a materially different work setup.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard University School of Law states that the library has wireless access throughout, oak tables equipped with data jacks and electrical outlets, computers on each floor, and a 52-seat computer training room.
cards.source_title: Vernon E. Jordan, Jr. Law Library | Howard University School of Law
cards.access_notes: Confirm current entry eligibility before visiting. The Law Library’s study rooms are restricted to current Howard Law and Divinity students.
